answer.policy_title: Surgery of the Ankle — UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange Medical Policy
answer.effective_date: July 1, 2026 (this is the version in force on the 2026-08-16 denial date; the policy PDF is copyrighted 2026 and labeled 'Effective 07/01/2026')
criteria_quotes: "Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP: Procedures: Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint); Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle; Arthrotomy, Ankle; Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle. Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."
Applicable Codes table lists: 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle — 27702 Arthroplasty, ankle; with implant (total ankle)' — confirming this policy is the one that governs CPT 27702.
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the date of the notice (2026-08-16), i.e., must be received by 2027-02-12, per the terms stated in the denial letter itself.
answer.submission_route: The excerpt of the denial letter provided does not itself contain the mailing address, fax number, or portal link for filing the appeal — only the 180-day deadline. Standard UnitedHealthcare/Oxford commercial channels for a member (or authorized provider) appeal of a medical-necessity ('UM') denial in New Jersey are: (1) a written appeal mailed or faxed to the address/fax printed on the actual denial notice (this is the address the patient should look for on the letter they received — it was not present in the text supplied to me); (2) submission through the member portal at myuhc.com; or (3) calling the member services number on the back of the insurance ID card to request the appeal form and confirm the correct submission address/fax. Because this is a New Jersey-regulated commercial/ACA plan, the plan is also subject to New Jersey's UM appeal ("Stage 1 UM Appeal") process rules, which the plan's own appeal instructions should reference.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The 'Surgery of the Ankle' policy does not itself spell out the specific medical-necessity criteria (e.g., required conservative-treatment duration, imaging findings, BMI limits, etc.) for CPT 27702/total ankle replacement. Instead, it incorporates by reference a separate, proprietary product: InterQual® CP: Procedures — 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle.' InterQual criteria are licensed clinical decision-support content (owned by a third party, currently Change Healthcare/Optum) and are not published openly on the web; the hyperlink in UHC's policy ('Click here to view the InterQual® criteria') routes to a restricted UHC provider-portal resource, not a public document. To get the actual criteria that were applied to this denial, the patient (or their physician) should: (1) request, in writing, a free copy of 'the specific rule, guideline, protocol, or other similar criterion relied upon in making the adverse determination,' which UHC/Oxford is required to provide under ACA claims-and-appeals regulations (29 CFR 2590.715-2719 / NJ equivalent); (2) ask the treating surgeon's office to pull the InterQual 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle' criteria via their UHC provider portal access, since providers can view InterQual content when performing prior-authorization reviews; and/or (3) call the number on the back of the member ID card and ask for the InterQual criteria used to deny reference number POC-3469ABE4FC-29435.
answer.notes: I located and directly verified the governing UHC/Oxford commercial policy document ('Surgery of the Ankle,' Policy Number 2026T0622O) that explicitly lists CPT 27702 under 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle' and states that medical-necessity determinations for this code are made against InterQual® CP criteria, not against text spelled out in the UHC policy itself. I was not able to retrieve the InterQual criteria text (it is proprietary/licensed content, not publicly indexed), and I could not confirm from the search results the exact mailing address/fax/portal instructions specific to this member's Oxford NJ commercial appeal — the denial-letter excerpt supplied to me did not include that information, so the patient should check the reverse/other pages of their actual letter or call member services to confirm the exact submission channel and address before mailing anything. I did not rely on non-authoritative third-party 'template' or blog sites for any factual claim in this answer, only on the UHC-hosted policy PDF I fetched directly.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Date of notice: 2026-08-16
Member: Cameron Carter
Member ID: W300143742
Plan: UnitedHealthcare / Oxford (Commercial/ACA), state of New Jersey

Dear Cameron,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Total ankle replacement
    Procedure code (CPT): 27702

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-12).

Reference number: POC-3469ABE4FC-29435
